Page 16 of 30 Approved for Public Release Another challenge of manufacturing the inner tank is with the mandrel. The mandrel will provide support for the fiber placement and define the tank inside surface/shape. However, after manufacturing, the mandrel has to be removed. With the small tank end openings, the mandrel removal will be challenging. The team is considering water soluble mandrel option for the prototype. Collapsible or bladder mandrel are considered to be more feasible options for tank production. Figure 20: An example of (a) a Filament winding process, and (b) Automated fiber placement process. Outer shell manufacturing: The outer shell is a two half-shell design. In overall tank assembly, the outer shell opens up and the inner tank and insulation materials such as multi-layer insulation (MLI) are placed in, and then the shell is closed. An insulative vacuum is pulled in the space between the outer shell and inner tank. To prevent shell buckling under vacuum, both composite laminate and sandwich (composite skin/core/composite skin) structures are considered as candidates for the outer shell. Since the shell is not expected to have concave surface features, AFP, FW, and even forming are considered potential manufacturing options. Insulation: Multi-Layer Insulation (MLI): The team worked with Aerospace Fabrication & Materials (AFM) on MLI materials for LH2 tank prototype. The MLI grades of interest are the standard grade PolaWrap® and premium grade PolaLoft™, as shown in Figure 21, to provide the balance of cost and performance. The MLIs are prefabricated stack up of ultrathin surface-aluminized polyester film reflector layers to provide efficient thermal insulation with minimal weight and stiffness. The premium grade has intentionally-designed crinkled layers to improve insulation efficiency and reduce weight. The insulation has two sections. One is in tape form with customized cut to wrap around the LH2 tank spherical domes smoothly. The other is in an MLI blanket form, cut to fit the middle cylinder of LH2 tank. The design of the MLI tape and blanket was in the final stage at program termination. Reference insulation performance is shown in Figure 22. Page 17 of 30 Approved for Public Release Figure 21. Insulation performance of various materials (Source: NASA Kennedy Space Center) Phase 1 cylindrical tank prototype manufacturing. Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) was finalized as the composite manufacturing method for fabricating the Phase 1 inner and outer tank prototypes. Multi-Layer Insulation (MLI) would be placed between the inner and outer tanks to provide insulation along with vacuum. An inter-tank support structure would also be placed between the inner and outer tanks to provide mechanical support as well as minimize heat conduction from outer to inner LH2 tank.
